tasks.short: Assess weather, fuel and maps when determining air routes

steps.what: Analyze weather reports, fuel requirements, maps and traffic constraints to determine suitable air routes

tasks.design: Retain controller interpretation of weather, flight information and maps within the {OTHER} air traffic planning environment. Existing route calculations can inform the assessment, but this design does not replace the controller's operational judgement or issue a clearance.
tasks.previous_blocker: A mathematically feasible route may conflict with actual traffic, coordination arrangements or changing conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital planning tools exist, but their availability alone does not establish a reduction in controller assessment time.
tasks.still_hard: The controller must understand uncertainty and reconcile information from pilots and adjacent sectors.
tasks.human_edge: The controller judges the operational relevance of constraints and recognises when a proposed route needs further coordination.
tasks.altitude: Route assessment and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain aircraft fuel and weather constraints affecting route choice
reach.learn: Difference between a planning calculation and an operationally acceptable route

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports flight planning against weather and airspace restrictions; that capability does not establish controller labour savings or authority to issue a clearance.
Retaining the controller's interpretation and coordination is a model-knowledge boundary for this task.

assumptions: Boundary ends at route assessment; issuing instructions, aircraft operation and dispatcher flight planning are separate tasks.

Meteorological services produce weather observations with times; flight planning staff and pilots provide aircraft, route and fuel information; existing airspace services provide map versions and restrictions. No automatically valid route flag is presumed.
All checking of provenance, interpretation, missing-data enquiries and coordination stays in s1 at full time. Existing manual procedures apply when information is unavailable.
Test native planning and display functions before custom code. OTHER denotes the existing air traffic planning environment.
No new integration or capture requirement is introduced, so additional upkeep is zero; existing planning runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Which route planning functions controllers actually use
Who supplies fuel information and how current it is
research_questions: Which route checks are already supported by native tools and still require operational interpretation?

already_counted.description: Route assessment, information checks and coordination

incremental.description: No additional system or capture upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental=0. No time is removed from interpreting weather, fuel information and traffic constraints; existing route calculation runtime is not labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile activity reports and retain aircraft message records

steps.what: Capture activity details and verify aircraft message records for the reporting period
Complete daily activity reports by arranging checked events and references to aircraft messages
Verify report meaning and message references, then sign and retain the accepted daily report

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} electronic strip and communication-record system to assemble a daily report from controller-checked events. Store the draft in {DOCS}; the controller verifies chronology, meaning and message references before signing and retaining it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Daily reports required re-entering events that were already represented in operational records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital records can populate fixed report sections once the controller has checked the source dataset.
tasks.still_hard: Logs can omit context, and a message recording cannot automatically establish the intended meaning of an unusual event.
tasks.human_edge: The controller explains operational significance and detects misleading or incomplete accounts.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into arranging reports; responsibility for their accuracy remains unchanged.

reach.task: Trace an operational event across control and airfield records

evidence.claim: Frequentis smartSTRIPS demonstrates electronic flight strips in operational towers, not automatic daily reports or measured reporting savings.
A configured daily report from checked strip and communication records is a model-knowledge design with unmeasured savings.

assumptions: Boundary is reporting and retaining references, not creating clearances, evaluating live traffic or recording radio audio at runtime.

The existing strip system records flight id, event time and operational entries; the communication system records channel, timestamp and recording reference. Controller entry and verification of report period, event category, narrative, source reference and missing details are fully counted in s1.

The report generator uses only the checked dataset from s1. No structured incident or completeness flag is assumed; unclear entries are resolved manually before generation, and missing exports keep the relevant copying manual.
Test native report configuration before a custom integration. OTHER denotes electronic strips and communication-record management; runtime logging itself earns no saving.
For a roll-up, count source capture once if another records-review task uses this same dataset. Retention and access settings require local confirmation and the stated upkeep allowance.
unknowns: Availability of source exports and stable message references
Whether daily reports are already generated
Local retention, access and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Can a native report reproduce a daily sample without losing event context or recording references?

already_counted.description: Capture and verification of report source fields
Semantic review, signing and retention checking

incremental.description: Maintain report mapping and investigate changed source formats
Records support maintains access and retention configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact daily report version, period, event narratives and message-reference snapshot verified in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 27. Range covers reports already generated and partial automation of copying; all source capture and semantic review remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review record clarity and completeness and maintain accepted records

steps.what: Review records against required-field lists and locate missing items or inconsistent references
Assess reports for clarity, reconcile omissions with authors and correct the record package
Verify and maintain the accepted record version with its required retention and access settings

tasks.design: Configure required-field and reference checks in the {OTHER} operational records system, using requirements maintained by the records officer. The controller checks meaning and resolves omissions, then confirms the exact corrected version and proposed retention and access settings in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical completeness checks and repeated record filing occupied attention alongside the harder clarity review.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record forms can flag absent fields and prefill retention settings without treating those checks as proof of compliance.
tasks.still_hard: A fully populated report can still misrepresent events or omit important context.
tasks.human_edge: The controller distinguishes a clear, faithful account from a superficially complete record.
tasks.altitude: Mechanical checks require less copying; accountability for clarity and acceptance remains unchanged.

reach.task: Translate approved record requirements into versioned form rules
reach.learn: Difference between completeness validation and substantive compliance

evidence.claim: Configured required-field checks and retention defaults can support record review, while substantive clarity remains a human judgement; this is an unmeasured model-knowledge design.

assumptions: Boundary begins after an author submits an operational record and ends at accepted maintenance; live activity capture is not repeated here. Source capture belongs to the report author's workflow, including task 12749 where applicable, and must be counted once in roll-ups.

Operational report authors produce record id, date, event fields, narrative and source references during their counted reporting work. The records officer produces a versioned list of required fields, accepted record types, retention categories and access groups; additional rule maintenance is counted as other-role upkeep.

s1 checks only the presence and cross-reference consistency of supplied fields. Unknown values are flagged without being invented; the controller contacts authors and captures corrections in fully retained s2.

s3 uses the corrected package from s2 and officer-maintained settings; checking the proposed settings and exact version remains in its 20 retained hours. If rules or configuration are missing, checks and maintenance stay manual.

Test native records configuration before custom code. OTHER means operational records management. Applicable national record duties require local confirmation; no US statutory rule is transplanted to Europe.
research_questions: Which missing fields can be flagged without falsely declaring a record substantively complete?

already_counted.description: Clarity review, author enquiries and correction capture
Verify exact accepted version and maintenance settings

incremental.description: Check changed forms and investigate validation exceptions
Records officer maintains versioned requirements and access rules

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected record package version and proposed retention and access settings reviewed in s3; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 23. Range covers already-configured forms and limited removal of repeated field checks; clarity review and all correction capture retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reports and record checks can take less clerical effort; operational route assessment and substantive record responsibility remain with the controller.
reach: Reconcile operational event sources with airfield colleagues
Work with records staff on versioned completeness rules
role.ambitious_version: A controller who produces traceable records without confusing mechanical completeness with operational accuracy.
